protocol.comparison: Same CV birth poses, initial speeds, lanes, routes, tau .7, desired speed 15.65, seed and safety. Only --eager-insert changes pending-birth scheduling. No clipping of scoring errors or dropping delayed vehicles.
protocol.selection: Use eager insertion only if development uncapped position MAE + 30m * missing native fraction improves, without reducing within-4m coverage; report full failed candidates too.

physical_errors.scope: One unambiguous spatial identity association at observed birth, then free-running native predictions. Position errors are NOT censored at the association gate. Missing native states remain missing; all eligible reference states stay in coverage denominators. Early initialization bins are separate from later prediction errors.

aggregate.split: development recording validation, 600–1000 seconds; final holdout not evaluated
aggregate.driven_by: Actual complete raw-video ATLAS CV boundary crossings, estimated lanes and box-projected lengths; no ground-truth vehicle arrivals or interior states passed into SUMO
aggregate.conditioning: Development-only NGSIM geometry and turn probabilities; independent RSM schedule; SUMO chooses safe insertion speed. This is an approximate baseline, not a validated physical twin.

N.scope: Unpaired traversal distributions, not individual-vehicle travel-time prediction error; both endpoints inside the validation window

S.scope: Unpaired traversal distributions, not individual-vehicle travel-time prediction error; both endpoints inside the validation window

sb_queue_count.definition: <0.5 m/s at three consecutive 1 Hz samples (>=2 s), SB upstream band 1090–1250 local ft, lateral -55–0 ft; not physical queue-tail length

limitations: Incomplete turn bays, bus layby and midblock driveways
Approximate two-stage RSM phasing; signal lamps not independently decoded
CV missed/fragmented tracks and boundary misses propagate into reconstruction
Conditional counts/travel-time distributions do not establish per-vehicle physical accuracy or field intervention effects
